sections.content: How many people are "finance and investment analysts and advisers"?

184,980 people

were counted on the census as "finance and investment analysts and advisers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Finance and investment analysts and advisers give advice to customers, (who may be individuals, companies or specialist groups), on the purchase of investments, insurance, mortgages, pensions and other financial services and products.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "finance and investment analysts and advisers", 20.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "finance and investment analysts and advisers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "finance and investment analysts and advisers" included:

  • legal professionals (other)
  • chemical scientists
  • project support officers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "finance and investment analysts and advisers" there were more men than women (60.2% compared with 39.8%).

This means "finance and investment analysts and advisers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 60.2% and women made up 39.8% of "finance and investment analysts and advisers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "finance and investment analysts and advisers" included:

  • undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants
  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors
  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "finance and investment analysts and advisers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "finance and investment analysts and advisers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "finance and investment analysts and advisers", 6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (87.7% compared with 12.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (84%) than self-employed (16%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Tower Hamlets, this is in the same region of London.
